title: Unbounded K-flat replacements from functorial flat resolutions
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] with a monoidal structure $(\otimes,\mathbf 1)$ [def-sfb-monoidal-category] whose tensor product is additive in each variable. Colimits are as in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]; countable coproducts mean colimits over countable discrete categories, and $\mathbf Z$-indexed colimits mean colimits over the ordered set $(\mathbf Z,\leq)$. Assume countable coproducts exist, $\mathbf Z$-indexed colimits exist and their colimit functor preserves short exact sequences, and tensoring on either side with any fixed object preserves both those coproducts and those colimits. A flat object means an object whose tensor functors on both sides preserve short exact sequences. Assume there is a functor $P:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ with flat values and a natural epimorphism $P\Rightarrow\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}$. For every unbounded cochain complex $K$ in $\mathcal C$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], there are a K-flat complex $Q$ [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso] and a quasi-isomorphism $q:Q\to K$.

source.place: first paragraph, existence of K-flat resolutions under the general monoidal hypotheses; supporting source code: WeilConjectures.FromJoel.CategoryTheory.Abelian.Flat.KFlat, lines 378–437

proof.text: Let $\mathcal P$ be the isomorphism-stable class of all two-sided flat objects. It contains zero, because additive tensor functors take zero to zero. It is closed under finite biproducts: tensoring with $F\oplus G$ is the biproduct of tensoring with $F$ and with $G$, and a finite biproduct of short exact sequences is short exact (kernels and cokernels of a block-diagonal morphism are the biproducts of the respective kernels and cokernels). The given epimorphism $P(M)\to M$ supplies a quotient cover of each object by this class.

source.place: Tag 06Y4, more-algebra-lemma-K-flat-resolution, first sentence of proof, verifying the hypotheses of the resolution-system lemma; the finite-biproduct argument is valid in any abelian category.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-subcategory-truncation-resolution-system] to this class and $K$. It gives, for $n\ge1$, bounded-above complexes $E_n$ of flat objects and strictly compatible quasi-isomorphisms $e_n:E_n\to T_n=\tau_{\le n}K$. The hypotheses are exactly those verified in step 1. In particular the compatibility is an equality of complex morphisms, so the augmentations form a natural transformation of sequential diagrams; compatibility only up to homotopy would not suffice here.

source.place: Tag 06Y4, more-algebra-lemma-K-flat-resolution, application of Derived Categories Tag 06XX (derived-lemma-special-direct-system).

proof.text: Extend both diagrams to the ordered set $\mathbf Z$ by setting $E_n=T_n=0$ for $n<1$, with zero maps into the first stage. Set $Q=\operatorname{colim}_{n\in\mathbf Z}E_n$ termwise. The differentials are the maps induced by the compatible differentials of the stages; their square is zero after precomposition with every colimit map and hence is zero by the universal property. For each degree $i$, the diagram $T_n^i$ is constantly $K^i$ with identity transitions once $n>\max(i,0)$. Its augmentation to $K^i$ is therefore a colimit cocone: any compatible family is uniquely determined by its value at one such stage. These identifications respect the differentials. Thus $\operatorname{colim}_n T_n\cong K$, and the colimit of $(e_n)$ gives a complex map $q:Q\to K$.

source.place: Tag 06Y4, more-algebra-lemma-K-flat-resolution, formation of the direct-limit map; the explicit zero extension uses only the integer-indexed colimits assumed by this item.

proof.text: For any $\mathbf Z$-diagram of complexes $A_n$, write $Z_n^i=\ker d_{A_n}^i$, $B_n^{i+1}=\operatorname{im}d_{A_n}^i$ and $H_n^i=Z_n^i/B_n^i$. Exactness of the colimit functor applied to $0\to Z_n^i\to A_n^i\to B_n^{i+1}\to0$ and $0\to B_n^{i+1}\to A_n^{i+1}\to A_n^{i+1}/B_n^{i+1}\to0$ identifies the kernel and image of the colimit differential with $\operatorname{colim}Z_n^i$ and $\operatorname{colim}B_n^{i+1}$. Apply it once more to $0\to B_n^i\to Z_n^i\to H_n^i\to0$ to obtain the natural identification $H^i(\operatorname{colim}A_n)\cong\operatorname{colim}H^i(A_n)$. Naturality follows from the induced kernel, image and quotient maps in these three short exact sequences. Apply this to $(e_n)$: every $H^i(e_n)$ is an isomorphism, including the zero stages, so their colimit is an isomorphism. With step 3 this says $H^i(q)$ is an isomorphism for every $i$, hence $q$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 06Y4, more-algebra-lemma-K-flat-resolution, direct-limit quasi-isomorphism assertion; expanded using only the assumed preservation of short exact sequences and the definition of cohomology.

proof.text: For each $n\ge1$, choose its upper bound $b_n$ and apply [lem-sfb-bounded-above-flat-kflat] to $E_n$: the terms are flat and all ambient colimit and tensor hypotheses are exactly the hypotheses of the item. Thus $E_n$ is K-flat. The added stages $E_n=0$ for $n<1$ are K-flat too, because tensoring with the zero complex gives the zero complex and hence sends every map to a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 06Y4, more-algebra-lemma-K-flat-resolution, bounded-above K-flat stages; Tag 064K is the ring-module analogue, with its project generalization used here.

proof.text: Let $s:L\to M$ be any quasi-isomorphism of unbounded complexes. Preservation of the integer-indexed colimits by tensoring with fixed objects, followed by interchange of two colimits, gives natural complex isomorphisms $Q\otimes L\cong\operatorname{colim}_n(E_n\otimes L)$ and $L\otimes Q\cong\operatorname{colim}_n(L\otimes E_n)$, and the analogous isomorphisms for $M$. For example, in degree $i$ the first identification is $\bigoplus_{a+b=i}(\operatorname{colim}_n E_n^a)\otimes L^b\cong\operatorname{colim}_n\bigoplus_{a+b=i}E_n^a\otimes L^b$: the interchange is obtained because maps out of either side are exactly families of maps from the summands compatible in $n$. On each summand the two differential components are $d_E\otimes1$ and $(-1)^a1\otimes d_L$, so the identification respects differentials, and the identical summand calculation respects $1\otimes s$. For the second identification the degree-$i$ objects are $\bigoplus_{a+b=i}L^a\otimes(\operatorname{colim}_n E_n^b)$ and $\operatorname{colim}_n\bigoplus_{a+b=i}L^a\otimes E_n^b$. Preservation of colimits by $L^a\otimes-$ and the coproduct universal property identify maps out of both with families of maps from $L^a\otimes E_n^b$ compatible in $n$. On this summand the differential components are $d_L\otimes1$ and $(-1)^a1\otimes d_E$; the two components agree under that identification, and $s\otimes1$ agrees summand by summand as well. Applying these constructions with $L$ replaced by $M$ gives the two target identifications. By step 5 and the definition of two-sided K-flatness, $E_n\otimes s$ and $s\otimes E_n$ are quasi-isomorphisms for every $n$. The cohomology calculation in step 4 shows their colimits are quasi-isomorphisms. Under these natural identifications they are $Q\otimes s$ and $s\otimes Q$. Hence $Q$ is K-flat, and together with $q$ from step 4 it satisfies the conclusion.
